moduleSummary: Covers how a new community-based organization (CBO) and its physical sites are brought into ECMS, how site staff and their qualifications are tracked, and how a site's open/closed status controls what a vendor can do downstream (enrollment, attendance, budgeting, invoicing).

scenarios.title: Creating a new CBO organization record
scenarios.description: DOE staff can set up a brand-new community-based organization in the system, recording its legal name, tax ID, and billing address so it can later be paid and tracked.
scenarios.statusNote: Demonstrated in the user guide, steps 1-3.

scenarios.title: Adding a physical site to a CBO
scenarios.description: A CBO's physical location (a classroom building, center, etc.) is recorded as a site linked back to the organization, including which borough and school district it's in, since those values later drive how enrollments at that site are labeled.
scenarios.statusNote: Demonstrated in the user guide, steps 4-5.

scenarios.title: Adding a main contact person for a site
scenarios.description: A named person (e.g., a Site Director) is recorded as the site's point of contact, with their title and basic details.
scenarios.statusNote: Demonstrated in the user guide, steps 6-7.

scenarios.title: Giving a vendor's staff member a portal login
scenarios.description: Once a site contact exists, that person can be given their own login to the separate vendor-facing portal, where they can then do their own day-to-day work (budgets, enrollments, attendance, invoices) without needing DOE staff to do it for them.
scenarios.who: Operations Analyst / ECMS Admin (setup); CBO staff (portal use)
scenarios.statusNote: Demonstrated in the user guide, steps 8-9.

scenarios.title: A single portal user needing access to both a CBO and a Family Child Care Network (FCCN)
scenarios.description: Some staff (e.g., a Network Director) oversee multiple boroughs' worth of family child care networks on behalf of one vendor. It's an open question whether one login can see both the CBO's sites and its associated family child care network sites, or whether that person needs a separate login for each, and how that person should appear as a single contact rather than duplicated across networks.
scenarios.who: Network Director / CBO staff with multi-network responsibilities
scenarios.statusNote: Tracked as an open provisioning question, not yet resolved or tested (task still open as of research).

scenarios.title: Marking a site as temporarily closed
scenarios.description: A site can be marked closed for a limited time (e.g., for a renovation or an emergency), with a closure date, a reason, and an expected reopening date on file.
scenarios.statusNote: Demonstrated in the user guide, step 10.

scenarios.title: Marking a site as permanently closed
scenarios.description: A site that will never reopen can be marked permanently closed, with a closure date and reason on file, and no reopening date since none is expected.
scenarios.statusNote: Demonstrated in the user guide, step 11.

scenarios.title: A temporarily closed site automatically reopening
scenarios.description: When a site's scheduled reopening date arrives, the system automatically updates its status back to open/active without anyone having to manually flip a switch.
scenarios.statusNote: Demonstrated in the user guide, step 12; automation confirmed in backend closure-object work.

scenarios.title: Keeping a full history of a site's closures and reopenings over time
scenarios.description: A site can be closed and reopened more than once over its lifetime, and the system is expected to keep a running history of every closure and reopening rather than only remembering the most recent one.
scenarios.statusNote: A history-keeping closure record was built and is used internally, but the client-facing user guide only shows the current status on the site itself and doesn't demonstrate reviewing the full closure history list.

scenarios.title: Preventing conflicting or overlapping closure entries
scenarios.description: Once a site has been marked permanently closed, staff shouldn't be able to add another closure (temporary or permanent) on top of it, and a closure that has already started shouldn't have its start date changed after the fact (only its reopening date can still be adjusted for a temporary closure).
scenarios.statusNote: These safeguards were built and tested, but an edge case remained where adding a temporary closure with an already-past reopening date could incorrectly wipe out an existing permanent closure; not demonstrated in the client-facing guide.

scenarios.title: A closed site blocking new child enrollments
scenarios.description: Once a site is closed (temporarily or permanently), staff can no longer enroll a new child there for any month on or after the closure, with enrollment automatically allowed again once the site reopens.
scenarios.statusNote: Called out in the user guide (step 5 callout, step 13) and confirmed by dedicated regression testing.

scenarios.title: A closed site blocking new budget creation
scenarios.description: A vendor cannot start a new budget for a site for any period after that site closed; budget creation opens back up automatically once the site is marked reopened.
scenarios.statusNote: Called out in the user guide step 13; matches the signed BRD requirement.

scenarios.title: A permanently closed site blocking invoices past the closure month
scenarios.description: For a site that has closed for good, a vendor can no longer submit invoices for any period after the closure month.
scenarios.statusNote: Called out in the user guide step 13; matches the signed BRD requirement.

scenarios.title: Attendance handling during a temporary closure
scenarios.description: During the month a site closes, staff can still record attendance for the rest of that month, but attendance is blocked for any month after the closure until the site reopens.
scenarios.statusNote: The underlying rule was built and confirmed through regression testing, but it isn't demonstrated in the client-facing user guide (which covers Enrollment/Budget/Invoice impacts of closure but not Attendance).

scenarios.title: Loading DOE's existing vendor/site records into ECMS before go-live
scenarios.description: Before the system goes live, DOE's existing spreadsheet of which vendors run which sites needs to be loaded into ECMS as a one-time bulk import, after which that spreadsheet is retired and ECMS becomes the single source of truth for vendor/site tracking.
scenarios.who: DOE / ECMS implementation team (one-time technical task)
scenarios.statusNote: Still in internal review at time of research; not yet demonstrated end-to-end or reflected in the user guide.

scenarios.title: Tracking each staff member's job details at a site
scenarios.description: Every person working at a site (or an unfilled position, tracked as a placeholder) has a staff record showing their role type, job title, teacher type, and their hire date for each specific program (2K, 3K, 4K, or infant/toddler classrooms).
scenarios.statusNote: Demonstrated in the user guide, steps 14 and 16.

scenarios.title: Tracking each staff member's education and credentials
scenarios.description: A staff member's education level, whether they hold a Child Development Associate credential and how many hours toward it they've completed, years of classroom experience, any in-progress certifications, and study plan dates are all recorded and visible on their record.
scenarios.statusNote: Demonstrated in the user guide, step 15; various display/validation bugs (negative numbers, duplicate values, hidden fields for some internal roles) were found and fixed during testing.

scenarios.title: Automatically updating a staff member's licensing/eligibility status from the state PETS system
scenarios.description: A staff member's active/eligible credential status is meant to update automatically based on a feed from the state's PETS system, without anyone at DOE or the CBO manually re-entering it.
scenarios.statusNote: Explicitly could not be tested — the team did not have access to a PETS integration environment to trigger or verify a live status update, so this remains unverified.

scenarios.title: Uploading supporting documents for a staff member's qualifications
scenarios.description: Supporting paperwork (education certificates, teaching certificates, study plans, certifications, etc.) can be attached directly to a staff member's record, and the system requires proof to be attached before certain qualification claims (like a completed certification) can be saved.
scenarios.statusNote: Demonstrated in the user guide, step 17; mandatory-upload enforcement and metadata/visibility bugs were found and fixed during testing.

scenarios.title: A vendor editing their own staff member's contact details
scenarios.description: A CBO user should be able to open and update the contact information for one of their own currently-active staff members.
scenarios.statusNote: An earlier defect blocked saving these edits with an error; this was fixed and confirmed working.

scenarios.title: Reviewing which budgeted staff positions are vacant across sites
scenarios.description: DOE and CBO staff can pull a point-in-time report showing which budgeted staff positions (including administrative and vacancy placeholder roles) are currently unfilled, grouped by organization and site, without having to check every staff record one by one.
scenarios.who: Operations Analyst / CBO staff with reporting access
scenarios.statusNote: The report exists and is referenced in the user guide (step 18) as the destination for staff data, but the report itself isn't screenshotted/walked through in the guide, and testing found (now-fixed) bugs where a vacancy type was missing from a dropdown, a vacant record was missing from the report, and duplicate rows appeared.

scenarios.title: Adding a new class directly from a site record
scenarios.description: A vendor should be able to add a new class for a site directly from that site's record in the vendor portal.
scenarios.statusNote: Reported as missing from the vendor portal's Site view; ticket was awaiting UAT confirmation at time of research, not yet confirmed fixed or reflected in the user guide.
